newsitem.title: UK: Storehouse jumps on sales increase.
newsitem.headline: Storehouse jumps on sales increase.

text.p: Shares in Storehouse Plc climbed on Thursday after the company said group sales had risen 14.5 per cent in the first quarter of the year, dealers said.
Storehouse shares jumped 13p to 201p by 1111 GMT in volume of 2.1 million shares.
Analysts said the trading statement from Storehouse was positive for the shares, and highlighted like-for-like sales growth from Mothercare and BHS as particularly encouraging.

Dealers added the shares were partly boosted by a bullish statement from electrical retailer Dixons Group Plc yesterday. Dixons said windfall cash from building society demutualisations had been used by consumers to boost sales of household appliances.
Shares in Storehouse had fallen to 183p on July 7, their lowest level for over four years, in a sector that has underperformed the rest of the UK equity market in recent months.
"The stock has bombed out of late but this could signal the turning point," said one dealer.
